stem: Vikram compares two class teams. Team P has $6$ players and scored $48$ points in all. Team Q has $8$ players and scored $56$ points in all. He wants a fair comparison of typical scoring when the teams have different sizes.

parts.text: Which claim correctly chooses a fair basis for the comparison?

options.text: Compare the per-player averages: Team P averages $8$ points and Team Q averages $7$ points.
Compare the totals only: Team Q scored $56$ and Team P scored $48$.
Compare the team sizes only: Team Q has $8$ players and Team P has $6$.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: The teams have different numbers of players, so a per-player average is a fair typical score; totals alone favour the larger team.

teacher.key_rationale: Different team sizes make totals unfair; per-player averages (8 vs 7) balance that. Totals or head-counts alone grab the largest printed feature instead of a fair typical score.
